title: Four Sherwood FOIA requests: records, responses and unresolved questions
summary: The selected records document substantial disclosure, later additions, changes to redactions, and unresolved questions about attachment and search coverage. They support specific follow-up inquiries, not a citywide compliance score or a finding of intentional withholding.

cases.title: Vehicle-specific ALPR captures and disclosure handling
cases.scope: ALPR captures, images, timestamps and locations for one specified Arkansas vehicle, June 1-July 1, 2026. The request asked for expedition because of the stated purge period and for justification if records were denied or redacted. The plate is withheld from this publication.
cases.status: July 14 portal snapshot: Completed. No present live-portal status is asserted.
cases.received: The July 1-labelled ZIP contains 85 files: 84 JPEGs and one CSV with 80 nonempty data rows, spanning 19 capture dates and 12 cameras. ZIP labels are download labels, not proof of delivery time.
cases.assessment: Substantial responsive image and structured-data production is demonstrated. All 80 CSV image-reference groups are represented after normalizing punctuation, milliseconds and numbered filename suffixes. The four additional JPEGs have different byte hashes; they are not established duplicates. The original disclosure authority and handling safeguards remain unresolved in the selected response materials.
cases.history: ARAP's July 14 clarification sought disclosure authority, verification, approval and preservation. The preserved email includes a delivery failure for one copied address. It does not establish delivery to every recipient or nonresponse by the whole City. Later screenshots repeat the inquiry, not a substantive City reply.
findings: 85 is the file count, not the count of detections or photographs. The earlier clarification's approximate 85-image/detection description should be corrected to 84 JPEGs and 80 CSV rows.

The 80 rows have 80 distinct exact date/time/camera combinations. The existing website's 74-event analysis applies a separate 60-second same-camera burst-collapse rule. It is a derived grouping, not the agency's raw count or proof that six rows are exact duplicates.

The July 14 letter says the requester did not assert vehicle ownership or consent and asks what authority supported release. That is the requester's statement, not proof that no other authorization existed. The original request itself does not assert ownership or consent.

This case concerns disclosure handling as well as completeness. Producing more identifying information is not inherently a better FOIA response. The public materials here omit the plate and do not republish the vehicle photographs.
cases.follow_up: Seek the existing release-authorization, verification, routing and review records; ask for the legal basis relied upon and any response to the July 14 inquiry. Verify delivery/rerouting of the failed copied address. Confirm whether the export covered the full requested period and distinguish no captures from deletion or filtering.
categories: Vehicle-specific images
Responsive records identified
84 JPEGs; 80 normalized image-reference groups match the CSV.
Reconciliation does not certify every capture held by the system.
Capture timestamps and locations
Responsive records identified
80 CSV rows, 19 dates, 12 camera labels; coordinates and descriptors are present.
An export's coverage/filters and receipt-time availability are not independently certified.
Disclosure authority and verification
Clarification unresolved
The request did not assert ownership/consent; July 14 inquiry asks for the release basis.
No substantive City answer is identified in the selected folder. Do not infer unauthorized release without resolving authority.
Preservation and response history
Partly documented
July 14 request and one copied-address delivery failure are preserved.
No preserved record here confirms City-wide receipt, preservation steps or final clarification response.

cases.title: Drone acquisition, integration, policies and authority
cases.scope: Nine categories concerning acquisition/financial documents; identifying equipment and funding; subscriptions; integration; communications; policies; third-party access; FAA authority; and training. Communications/development period begins January 1, 2025 and runs through processing. Native format is requested when reasonably available.
cases.status: August 18 portal snapshot: Submitted. August 21 City email says work continued and promises another update by Monday afternoon. These are historical snapshots, not proof of current status or completion date.
cases.received: August 26-labelled ZIP: 24 files (21 PDFs, two DOCX, one TXT). October 5-labelled ZIP: 58 files (50 PDFs, five MSG, two DOCX, one TXT). The later archive retains all 24 initial filenames: 18 byte-identical, six byte-changed, plus 34 added filenames. The extracted August-labelled folder is not an accurate snapshot of the 24-file ZIP.
cases.assessment: The archive comparison credits additional disclosure: contracts/quotes, policies, FAA material, installation, integration and communications are present. It also identifies new obscuring in replacement versions. Filename/date and file-count changes must not be misreported as a count of new emails, unique records or deliberate omissions.
cases.history: The August 21 status email is affirmative evidence the City communicated ongoing work. Both dated archives are preserved. The selected records do not establish why the batch changed, when each item was uploaded, whether the 58-file archive was final, or the City’s field-specific rationale for added obscuring.
findings: The later archive adds 34 filenames, removes none, changes six and retains 18 byte-for-byte. Six changed files are five quote/proposal PDFs and Drone Emails 2-Redacted.pdf. Both versions of each changed file retain the same page count.

In each of five quote/proposal PDFs, pages 7-10 render fully black in the later archive where the earlier versions displayed BRINC product material. These are 20 page instances, not 20 distinct underlying documents. Page 11 also changes in each file; the inspected example obscures a brochure photograph. The reason and legal basis are not established by the comparison.

Drone Emails 2 differs visually on pages 22, 23, 31, 33, 36 and 39. Examples include obscuring an equipment line and resource URLs. Do not republish previously exposed resource links or infer a motive from the later treatment.

The later archive contains native MSG files, so a statement that Sherwood produced only scanned PDFs would be inaccurate. Many substantial email compilations are image-based PDFs. Their searchability and attachment completeness remain separate questions.

The signed two-page agreement incorporates a Motorola Customer Agreement by reference. Two separately downloaded October 20 web versions of that agreement are research references, not CITY-2026-150 production files or proof of the controlling terms at signing.

Two native emails in this archive concern the handling of CITY-2026-164. They are cross-request evidence, not part of that nine-file ZIP. The routing email also records a staff assertion that the requester waived three business days; this review has not located the underlying agreement and does not adopt that assertion as independently verified.
cases.follow_up: Ask for an itemized explanation of the replacement versions and applicable exemptions, the relationship between the dated batches, any final response and processing cutoff, available native/searchable email exports with attachments, the terms/version incorporated at signing, and outstanding financial, access and training records. Credit records already produced rather than asking for them as if absent.
categories: 1. Acquisition and financial records
Partial / records identified
Quotes, signed agreement, interface proposal and electrical estimate appear.
Not a demonstrated complete purchase-order, invoice, payment, grant and budget trail.
2. Equipment, vendor, price, delivery and funding
Partial / records identified
Quotes, agreement and installation records identify equipment, vendor and commercial terms; infrastructure budget email adds funding context.
Distinguish quotes from payments, planned dates from delivery, and departmental understanding from final ledger entries.
3. Software and service subscriptions
Partial / records identified
Quote/service material and signed agreement are supplied.
Identify controlling incorporated terms and any separate subscriptions; do not substitute later web downloads for executed terms.
4. Integration capability
Responsive records identified; deployment scope unresolved
Integration questions, CAD/interface documents, invitations and talking paper appear.
Capability or planned integration does not establish an actual ALPR-triggered drone launch.
5. Program communications
Partial / later additions documented
Email compilations and later MSG files document implementation and coordination.
Date/custodian coverage and attachment/native completeness remain unverified. Added filenames are not a count of individual emails.
6. Current or proposed policies
Responsive records identified
October 2025 policy, May 2026 working copy and January addendum appear.
Which version was operative when, adoption history and completeness of related policies require clarification.
7. Third-party access permissions
Partial / records identified
Talking paper, police/fire MOU and LiveOps/support coordination identify intended roles or categories.
Not a complete effective permission roster or account-access audit; a proposed arrangement is not proof of actual access.
8. FAA registrations and operating authority
Responsive records identified
Registration and Part 91 waiver/COA materials appear.
Authority is conditional; no finding here certifies every operation or resolves amendments and full applicable conditions.
9. Training materials and personnel counts
Partial / records identified
Authorized-operator letter and training/onboarding references appear; related credentials are in CITY-164.
Certification, proposed seats, attendance and completed BRINC-specific training are distinct. Cross-request credentials do not prove complete response to this category.
Format, redactions and batch disposition
Unresolved explanation / demonstrated changes
PDF/DOCX/TXT and later MSG formats; six changed filenames including black-rendering pages.
Obtain applicable exemptions and explanation of replaced versions; no legal determination from black rendering alone.

cases.title: Citywide drone-program communications and attachments
cases.scope: Email communications, associated invitations and attachments, January 1, 2025-August 27, 2026, concerning DFR procurement, review, signing, funding, installation, operation, integration and council knowledge. The request expressly includes the Mayor's Office, legal counsel, IT, finance, purchasing and other City personnel. It is not an unrestricted request for all standalone records or every Slack/text message.
cases.status: August 27 portal snapshot: Submitted. The October 21 requester email describes the request as completed and unable to accept portal correspondence. That statement is preserved, but no later portal snapshot or City completion notice is in the selected folder.
cases.received: October 5-labelled ZIP: nine PDFs totaling 26 pages. One 16-page email compilation, seven pilot credential PDFs and one recurrent-course certificate. All nine PDFs lack extractable text. The 16-page compilation reproduces two forwarded chains concerning onboarding/training; earliest substantive email in those chains is August 11, 2026.
cases.assessment: This ZIP documents implementation, training arrangements and credentials but does not establish the requested early procurement, mayoral/legal-review, signing-authority or council-notification communication history. Stronger, specific leads are the expressly referenced COA-BVLOS and class-instructions attachments absent from this ZIP, and in-range infrastructure communications actually supplied in CITY-150.
cases.history: The initial CITY-164 folder contained ARAP's October 21 clarification but no substantive City answer. CITY-2026-198 subsequently supplied an October 21 internal response from Capt. Edwards and the FOIA Coordinator's broader routing to City recipients. Those developments are credited; completed searches and each category's disposition remain unverified. The reproduced account of the Mayor's statements is still the requester's account, not an independent speech transcript.
findings: The original request expressly reaches City personnel regardless of department. Its subject is Citywide even though records were handled through police. A police response alone does not establish the City failed to search other offices.

Cross-request routing email: August 27, 07:47, Williams asks Edwards/Perez to review and be specific about documentation not held; Edwards forwards to Snyder/Spears around 08:13; Snyder replies around 08:18 that he does not think IT/Facilities must reply and will seek Williams's confirmation. This documents an initial interpretation and proposed clarification, not the outcome of the search.

The July 21-22 infrastructure-expense chain supplied in CITY-150 involves Edwards, Snyder and Spears and discusses IT/Facilities budget responsibility. Its date, participants and subject fit CITY-164. It is absent from the selected nine-file CITY-164 ZIP. Whether it was supplied by reference, through another channel, or omitted remains unresolved.

On compilation page 10, Perez states that the Part 91 COA-BVLOS is attached. On page 11, he states that the response to Class Instructions is attached. Pages 12-13 refer to an unreadable attachment, resend and request letter. These are concrete attachment leads, not proof of current retention or intentional withholding.

A Part 91 document was already supplied in CITY-150's initial ZIP. Its presence elsewhere mitigates a claim that the City never provided FAA material, but does not prove it is the exact attachment referenced in the CITY-164 email or that the later response explained the cross-reference.

The January 2025 recurrent-course certificate is an older credential. It must not be counted as a January 2025 procurement email. Labels '(42)' and '(43)' on forwarding messages are not proof that 41 responsive emails were withheld.
cases.follow_up: Seek the referenced COA and class-instruction/request-letter attachments with parent-email metadata; reconcile the July infrastructure chain and earlier CITY-150 communications; confirm offices, accounts, dates and systems searched; obtain the outcome of IT's routing clarification and any final City response. Ask for missing categories or applicable exemptions without presuming mayoral or legal records exist.

No legal-review chain or actual COA attachment in this ZIP; external-policy/FAA records elsewhere do not establish complete communications coverage.

Native/searchable format and metadata
Format shortcoming; availability unresolved
Nine image-based PDFs, no native emails in this ZIP.
Native/searchable export was preferred where practicable. Availability and conversion limits are not established.
Citywide search coverage and routing
Initial routing documented; final coverage unresolved
CITY-150 native email shows Williams to police, then Edwards to IT/Facilities and Snyder's clarification plan.
Does not establish all requested offices were searched or excluded; seek actual outcome and existing search records.
No-records/exemption/retention explanations and follow-up
Not identified in selected CITY-164 ZIP
October 21 clarification seeks category-specific answers and supplementation.
CITY-198 now supplies an internal substantive City response and broader routing. A final category-by-category disposition and completed office-search results remain unverified.

cases.title: Drone activity, telemetry, recording metadata and access audits
cases.scope: Existing records from earliest installed-system activity through receipt: flight/attempt logs, system activity, CAD, roles, telemetry, recording metadata, access audits, safety/exception events, airspace restrictions and existing activity/outcome reports. Underlying video/images were expressly excluded.
cases.status: October 13 portal snapshot: Completed; all four listed uploads dated October 9. Request receipt hour/timezone is not shown.
cases.received: October 13-labelled ZIP: four files, three PDFs and one XLSX. Independent earlier recount: 218 summary rows (216 positive duration), 562 page-access events, 550 Auth event IDs, and 12 share-link rows. These count different things and cannot be added as flights or people.
cases.assessment: Partial coverage is established, but no identifiable CAD/dispatch production, detailed path/altitude/distance telemetry, comprehensive recording lifecycle metadata, safety/airspace event records or broader outcome reports. No category disposition or field-specific redaction rationale is visible in the selected request snapshot and productions.
cases.history: Request scope runs through receipt, unlike CITY-150's through-processing communications scope. Summary dates end October 7 and its timezone is CDT/UTC-5. Auth includes two printed October 8 events. Audit/share timezones and export filters are not specified. Filenames and export endpoints are not proof of a missing day.
findings: The Flight Log is a page-access export: 356 show, 197 mission, eight sync video view and one diagram. Twenty-eight events lack exit/duration. These are not 562 flights, proof of viewing, or unique sessions.

The summary has 218 rows, two zero-duration and six blank call types. Redacted identifiers prevent independent flight/case deduplication. The prior approximately 33.9-hour total is not independently certified and is not adopted as an exact figure.

Auth has 550 distinct event IDs, including two dated October 8 in the printed timezone. Removing those leaves 548 printed-date-through-October-7 events, not a confirmed receipt-bounded total. Successful login / False must not automatically be treated as a failed password attempt.
ShareLink has 12 rows: 10 expired, two revoked; configured lifetimes total 21.5 hours, not actual viewing time. There is no recipient/viewer/download field.

The portal describes the Flight and Auth PDFs as redacted copies of XLSX files. Available native exports are a concrete follow-up. PDF was permitted, so conversion alone is not proof of a statutory violation.
cases.follow_up: Resolve category dispositions, retention and earliest availability, preservation, actual receipt/export boundaries, available native files and redaction bases before mission-specific interpretation. Seek existing telemetry, CAD, recording lifecycle, safety/airspace and outcome records or clear no-records/exemption/custodian responses.
categories: Logs for every launch or attempted launch, with times, duration, type, identifiers, locations, roles, reason and outcome [R p. 1]
Partial
S1 pp. 1-6 supplies dates/times, duration, User, Launch Address, drone/org names and Call Type. Flight ID, Location and Case ID are redacted.

Partial. No explicit attempt status, disposition/outcome, destination, separate dock or crew-role fields. Six blank call types; two zero-duration rows. Case/flight joins unavailable. Confirm whether start/end are launch/recovery times and whether aborted attempts are included.
System activity documenting launches, deployments, missions, attempts/aborts, cancellations, returns and completed flights [R p. 1]
Partial
S1 completed-looking rows; S2 page visits.
Partial. S2 is not a launch-state history. No identifiable cancellation/abort/return event export or status-transition history. Zero-duration rows cannot automatically be classified as aborts.
CAD/dispatch association and initiation method [R p. 1]
Not identified as a separate CAD/dispatch production
Call Type in S1; Case ID withheld.
Not identified as a separate CAD/dispatch production. A classification is not a CAD history. Need CAD/event records and existing automated/dispatcher/officer/pilot initiation fields, if maintained.
Who initiated, authorized, approved, piloted, supervised or remotely assisted each flight [R p. 1]
Partial
S1 User; S2 access accounts; S3 authentication accounts.
Partial. User/access/login does not establish pilot in command, authorizer or remote assistant. No role-linked mission authorization history identified.
Flight history/telemetry: paths, altitude, distance, duration and launch/landing coordinates [R p. 1]
Partial
S1 duration and textual launch address.
Partial. No identifiable paths, altitude, distance, landing coordinates or comparable detailed telemetry. A launch address is not the flight route or destination.
Existing recording metadata: capture, retention/deletion, evidence transfer, case association, livestream and availability [R pp. 1-2]
Partial
S2 includes eight sync video view page visits; S4 shows share-link creation/expiration settings.

Partial. No comprehensive capture/recording inventory, deletion/retention/evidence-transfer history or per-mission metadata. Access/share capability does not establish capture, retention, actual viewing or transfer. No underlying media requested.
Audit/activity logs of access to missions, live/recorded video, histories and records, with user/time/action/access type [R p. 2]
Partial
S2 562 events; S3 550 authentication events; S4 12 link rows.

Partial. General login is not mission access. show/mission labels need definitions. No identifiable viewer/recipient/download/export lifecycle audit. 28 S2 rows lack exit/duration; redactions block joins. Confirm all relevant event types and systems were searched.
Failed/aborted launches, emergency landings, comms/GPS/navigation/geofence/Remote ID/collision and safety exceptions [R p. 2]
Not identified in supplied production
No dedicated exception log identified.
Not identified in supplied production. Need existing exception records or category-specific search/no-records explanation. Cannot infer zero safety events from silence.
Flights restricted/delayed/cancelled/rerouted/prevented by FAA/LAANC/BVLOS/weather/airports/TFRs or other airspace restrictions [R p. 2]
Not identified in supplied production
None identifiable.
Not identified in supplied production. Need responsive event records if held, or category-specific explanation. A training or test label does not answer this request.
Existing daily/weekly/monthly/cumulative reports or dashboards of activity/outcomes [R p. 2]
Partial
S1 is a summary table of individual rows.

Partial. No other identifiable dashboard/report with deployments, response times, cancellations, arrests, apprehensions, search outcomes or other attributed results. Do not demand a newly calculated report.
Native or ordinary system-exported electronic format where readily available, including CSV/XLSX/JSON/PDF; avoid screenshots/individual printing [R p. 2]
Unresolved format shortcoming
Three PDFs and one XLSX. R p. 4 describes S2 and S3 as redacted copies of XLSX originals.

Unresolved format shortcoming. Native tabular versions of S2/S3 appear to have existed based on portal descriptions; S1 is image-based and split horizontally. PDF was explicitly permitted, so PDF delivery alone is not proof of a violation. Ask for available redacted native exports or an explanation of availability/conversion limits.
Preserve existing rolling/deletion-prone records; identify retention and earliest date available at receipt [R pp. 2-3]
Unresolved
No retention/preservation explanation visible.
Unresolved. Production dates/ranges do not establish retention settings, receipt-time availability or preservation steps. No evidence here proves destruction, before or after receipt.
Rolling production and supplementation [R p. 3]
Unresolved
Four listed files uploaded October 9; snapshot later says Completed.
Unresolved. Snapshot does not show whether anything remained under review, whether supplementation was planned, or whether other correspondence explained completion.
Segregable remainder, specific statutory basis for each withholding/redaction, and category no-records response [R p. 3]
Partial disclosure; rationale unresolved
Visible redactions across S1-S4; no explanatory basis in supplied six-file record.

Partial disclosure; rationale unresolved. Request field/category-specific bases, extent of withholding and each category's disposition. No-records statements and search descriptions may exist elsewhere; this review has not seen them.

supplement.effect: City internal response/broader routing now credited; search results and procurement authority unresolved.
